findings.title: Device allow_batch bypasses the exact-Calculator single-answer gate for pid-only EXECUTE ops
findings.scenario: Workstation-approved (non-remote) Mission whose plan contains pid-targeted computer.focus_window {pid:5151} and computer.invoke_control {pid:5151, automationId:num8Button/num9Button} (no title, no Calculator window). The first EXECUTE ask gets a batchOffer (requestBatchable -> calculatorOperation accepts pid-only ops), so the remote verdict is batchOnly. A paired device's allow_once is refused ('computer.focus_window is not an exact reviewed Calculator operation'), but allow_batch is accepted: deviceRequestRefusal returns null for any allow_batch with a batchOffer for non-Agent Missions (line 2048-2049) before the remoteExecutionRefusal/scope/skill checks run. respond() then sets approvedOnce for the ask and creates a batch, and all three planned pid-targeted operations execute (probe: EXECUTED focus_window pid 5151, invoke_control num8Button, invoke_control num9Button; batch createdBy device:phone, usedCount 3, mission completed). The same early return also means a skill-step ask (refused at line 2051 for single answers) is batch-approvable by code reading. The same probe with a device-approved (remote) envelope gets no batch offer and is refused, so the bypass is limited to workstation-approved envelopes that a device supervises.
findings.evidence: Probe (throwaway, mkdtemp under OS temp, removed): ASK computer.focus_window risk EXECUTE reason 'EXECUTE actions were not approved for this mission.' batchOffer actions [computer.focus_window, computer.invoke_control]; REMOTE VERDICT {answerable:true,batchOnly:true}; allow_once by device:phone -> 'Approval required on Windows Host ... computer.focus_window is not an exact reviewed Calculator operation'; allow_batch by device:phone ACCEPTED; EXECUTED all 3 ops; events authorization.granted 'allow_batch by device:phone'. Root-cause code: manager.server.ts:2044 comment claims the batch is 'Calculator-bound by construction', but batches.server.ts:97 requestBatchable uses calculatorOperation (batches.server.ts:55-64), which accepts a pid with no title; the exact-identity predicate remoteCalculatorOperation (authorization.server.ts:238-239, requires title==='Calculator') is never applied to batch answers. Once approvedOnce is set, decide()'s oneTime allow (authorization.server.ts oneTime branch) skips scopeViolation for the executed op. Bounded impact: focus/invoke of CALCULATOR_CONTROLS automation ids on pid-identified windows, only for the workstation-approved plan's own digest-bound ops; no code/shell execution (terminal/provider/Git remain refused). Agent cross-app consents take the same branch and were not probed. Regression coverage gap: remote-authority tests (F01-R18) and the T9R-F01 approval-batches block exercise single answers, not pid-only batch offers.
findings.recommendation: Apply the exact-identity rule to batch answers: for a device allow_batch (and for batch eligibility when the request is device-visible), require every batch operation to satisfy remoteCalculatorOperation (title==='Calculator' or open_app app calculator) and run remoteExecutionRefusal plus the skill refusal per batch operation before returning null; or make requestBatchable/batchOffer require the Calculator title for remote answers. Do not let allow_batch set approvedOnce for a non-Calculator op. Correct the comment at manager.server.ts:2044. Add a regression test: workstation-approved plan with pid-only focus/invoke ops, device allow_batch must be refused and nothing executes.

findings.title: Device one-time answer carries into same-action verification checks, which skip the envelope scope check
findings.scenario: Non-Agent Mission whose envelope projectRoots is [project]. A user ask_every_time rule covers filesystem.read. The plan has an execute step filesystem.read on an in-project path A and a verification check filesystem.read on path B outside the project (verification READ checks are not root-scoped at approval; scopeFor only adds the project root). A paired device answers the execute ask. deviceRequestRefusal judges only the executor's params (lines 2054-2058), so path A passes. respond() sets step.approvedOnce={requestId, action:'filesystem.read'} (line 3702). The step runs and verifyAndComplete (line 2971) calls bus.request for check B. capabilityRequest sets oneTimeAction='filesystem.read' (line 1520), and approvedOnce is not cleared until completion (line ~3160). In decide(), the oneTime allow at authorization.server.ts:354 returns before scopeViolation at line 367, so the out-of-envelope read of B runs without any ask. The round-4 verify-phase judgement (E) covers only answers given in the verify phase, not this carry-over.
findings.evidence: Throwaway probe, decide() with a remote (device) envelope, roots=[project], filesystem.read of C:/Windows/win.ini: oneTime=false returns ask 'outside the approved read scope'; oneTime=true returns allow. The full mission path was not run end to end. Preconditions: a user ask_every_time rule on a READ action and a non-Agent Mission. Agent Missions are protected because agenticViolation (decide line 349) is checked before oneTime.
findings.recommendation: Judge every verification check that shares the device-approved action in the execute-phase candidate set, as the verify branch already does. Alternatively, clear approvedOnce when a step enters 'verifying' for a device answer, or bind oneTime to the approved params digest so it cannot cover a different check.

findings.title: Execution-config classifier false positives: any *.props/*.targets file and any directory named gradle
findings.scenario: Ordinary project files are classified as execution config. The regex alternative [^/\\]+\.(csproj|vbproj|fsproj|vcxproj|sln|props|targets) matches any file ending in .props or .targets, and EXECUTION_CONFIG_DIR (line 203) matches any directory named gradle. A paired-device filesystem.write to src/theme.props or src/gradle/x.ts is therefore refused as desktopRequired, even in a non-MSBuild or non-Gradle project.
findings.evidence: Probe via remoteExecutionRefusal('filesystem.write', {path}, 'WRITE', project): src/theme.props and src/gradle/x.ts return the 'configures Git, package scripts, hooks or tasks' desktop refusal. src/config.ts, src/props.ts, scripts/build.ts and src/index.ts return null. Fail-closed, so the impact is extra workstation prompts, not escalation; the Host-wide review gate still covers any code run over the file.
findings.recommendation: Limit props/targets to Directory.Build.* and files that real MSBuild projects import, and drop the bare 'gradle' directory name in favour of the Gradle file names already listed.

findings.title: Dotenv files are not execution config under the classifier
findings.scenario: EXECUTION_CONFIG_FILE has no entry for .env or .env.* files. A paired-device filesystem.write to src/.env (or .env) is not refused on the classifier. Whether a .env file can alter which program or runtime option a later command uses (for example Bun's automatic .env loading) was not verified. The later-run review gate would still apply to any code run afterwards.
findings.evidence: Probe: remoteExecutionRefusal('filesystem.write', {path:'src/.env'}, 'WRITE', project) and the bare .env path both return null; executionConfigPath returns false for both.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether .env* counts as execution config for the runtimes this Host launches (Bun, Vite, Node loaders) and add it to the classifier if so.

result.reasoning:
Not refuted. I reproduced it with a throwaway probe in an mkdtemp folder under the OS temp dir (deleted afterwards). Setup: a workstation-approved Mission with three pid-only ops (computer.focus_window {pid:5151}, two computer.invoke_control {pid:5151, automationId:num8Button/num9Button}), origin workstation, approved by workstation. Observed: the first ask is computer.focus_window EXECUTE with batchOffer [focus_window, invoke_control]. deviceRequestRefusal(req,"allow_once") returns the "not an exact reviewed Calculator operation" refusal. deviceRequestRefusal(req,"allow_batch") returns null. respond(req.id,"allow_batch","device:phone") is accepted, and all three ops execute with pid 5151. The batch record shows createdBy device:phone, usedCount 3, and the mission completes. The path is reachable in production: remoteVerdicts projects batchOnly:true for the request.

Root cause: manager.server.ts:2048-2049 returns null for any device allow_batch with a batchOffer (non-Agent) before the remoteExecutionRefusal/skill/scope checks at 2051-2066. The batch eligibility in batches.server.ts:97 uses calculatorOperation, which accepts pid-only ops. The exact-identity predicate remoteCalculatorOperation is at authorization.server.ts:159-161, not 238-239 as the finding states, and it is not applied to batch answers. This contradicts the owner policy that devices may approve only "exact reviewed Calculator ops naming the Calculator window", and it is an inconsistency with the single-answer path, which refuses the same op.

Severity is held at HIGH for the policy carve-out violation and the EXECUTE authority expansion, not BLOCKER. Impact is bounded: focus and invoke of CALCULATOR_CONTROLS automation ids on a pid window that the workstation plan names, with no code or shell execution. The skill-step claim was checked by reading code only (line 2048 precedes the skill check at 2051), not probed. I did not run the remote-authority test suite; the repo was not modified and git status is unchanged.

The core observation is real but the HIGH severity and the "arbitrary pid focus/invoke on pid-identified windows" impact are not.

Confirmed by code reading:
- manager.server.ts:2048-2049: deviceRequestRefusal returns null for any allow_batch with a batchOffer when consent is null (non-Agent Mission), before the step-skill check (2051) and remoteExecutionRefusal/scope checks (2060-2067). So a device allow_batch on pid-only EXECUTE ops is accepted while allow_once on the same op is refused.
- batches.server.ts:55-64 calculatorOperation accepts a pid with no title (line 62 requires title or pid), so requestBatchable/batchOffer admit pid-only ops. The single-answer predicate remoteCalculatorOperation (authorization.server.ts:159-160) requires title === "Calculator", and it is not applied to batch answers. The inconsistency is real.

Why the impact is bounded (the finding did not account for this):
- Batch execution is Calculator-only at runtime. In computer.server.ts, Find-Window with $batch set calls Assert-BatchWindow (line ~67-70), which calls Native-CalculatorFrame (requires Name -eq 'Calculator', Calculator package path and session checks) and throws for any non-Calculator window. focus_window (line ~308-336) calls Assert-BatchWindow directly. invoke_control calls Find-Window then Assert-BatchControl (line 224-230), which requires num0Button-sibling buttons and foreground match.
- Batch admission also runs prepareBatchAction (computer.server.ts ~529-541) via bus.server.ts:226-245. A non-Calculator pid makes Find-Window throw, identity is null, and the batch ends as scope_mismatch with a fresh ask (bus.server.ts:241-250). Admission fails closed.
- Batch ops are digest-bound to the workstation-approved plan (consultBatch, batches.server.ts:196-215), and batchOffer covers only the computer family, so no shell, terminal, provider, Git or code path is reachable.

So the realistic effect is that a device can trigger the workstation-planned Calculator operations that its single-answer path would refuse. That is a consistency gap against the owner rule "exact reviewed Calculator ops naming the Calculator window", and the comment at manager.server.ts:2044 is inaccurate about calculatorOperation alone. It is not a device-driven code-execution or arbitrary-window issue, so I rate it LOW rather than HIGH. The "same early return lets skill-step asks be batch-approved" point is also limited to the same Calculator-bound computer ops. Probes were not run and no repo files were touched.

Partially refuted as stated; the residual is real but low severity. The headline scenario (an out-of-envelope read of a path outside the project runs) cannot happen. A device answer never extends roots: manager.server.ts:1507 sets `once` only when `isTrustedLocalActor(answeredBy)`, so the verification check's `roots` stay `envelope.projectRoots` (line 1510). The filesystem adapter then calls `scopedPath(cwd, path, context.roots)` (capabilities/local.server.ts:57; paths.server.ts:35-38), which throws "Path is outside the approved scope" for any path outside the project. So the oneTime allow at authorization.server.ts:354 only skips decide()'s own checks. Those checks are the scopeViolation at line 367, the ask_every_time grant, the alwaysAsk risk classes, the riskClasses membership, and the sensitive flag. The remote execution classifier at decide() (before oneTime) and the agenticViolation check still apply. Residual: a single device one-time answer on filesystem.read (or filesystem.write) for path A lets a same-action verification check on an in-project path B, which is inside the reviewed plan, run without the workstation's ask_every_time or alwaysAsk prompt. filesystem.read manifests (local.server.ts:36-38) are READ and not sensitive or hardApproval. Code execution is not reachable: the device gate (manager.server.ts:2028-2068) refuses code-capable actions, and the carry-over only applies to the same action. Agent Missions are protected by agenticViolation ordering. This is a minor deviation from the exact-step binding, not a device-caused code execution or an out-of-envelope action, so it is LOW rather than MEDIUM. Verified by code reading only; no probe run, no repo tests run, no files changed.

findings.title: Review approval acknowledges paired-device changes the workstation was never shown
findings.scenario: Two manifestations, both probed against the real MissionManager/CapabilityBus. (a) Truncated disclosure: the review reason lists only the first 12 changed paths and then 'and N more' (bus.server.ts:170, manager.server.ts:1430), but pendingRemoteReview() returns the ids of every pending change (manager.server.ts:2273) and respond() acknowledges all of them (manager.server.ts:3594). Probe: phone-approved 12 benign writes plus build.mjs as the 13th change; the workstation's 'node build.mjs' review said 'and 1 more' with build.mjs not named; allow_once left pending=0 and the device-authored build.mjs wrote ran.txt. (b) Superseded re-ask: a device write between the ask and the workstation's answer makes the answer throw 'a fresh request lists the changes' (manager.server.ts:2335), but the re-ask keeps the stale reason text (split at manager.server.ts:3582 leaves the old 12-path list) while setting remoteReview to the full current id list (3583). Probe: R2 reason named only note01.txt; R2 remoteReview length was 2 including build.mjs; allow_once acknowledged build.mjs unseen and node build.mjs executed device-authored content. Once acknowledged, later runs of that file are not re-prompted.
findings.evidence: Probe scripts (deleted) ran via node --experimental-strip-types against C:/Users/allam/Documents/new/bun-router/src/lib. Outputs: 'pending device changes: 13 ... ask reason: ... (note01.txt ... note12.txt and 1 more)', 'build.mjs named in reason: false', 'pending device changes after workstation answer: 0', 'ran.txt: device-authored content executed'. Second probe: 'R1 answer result: Project files changed after this request was raised; a fresh request lists the changes.', 'R2 remoteReview: 2', 'R2 reason: ... note01.txt). Review them before allowing.', 'R2 names build.mjs: false', 'pending device changes after R2 answer: 0', 'ran.txt: device-authored content executed'. Repo test file remote-authority.test.ts still passes 49/49 because it only checks a single-change list (F01-R20).
findings.recommendation: Acknowledge only the change ids the approver was actually shown, or refuse allow_once whenever the displayed list is truncated (require the full list or a review step that lists every path). On a superseded re-ask, rebuild the reason from the current pending paths rather than splitting the old text, and never set remoteReview to ids the new reason does not show. Make mission-level listing (remoteChanges, manager.server.ts:2250-2258) include non-succeeded attempts too, since their ids are acknowledged as well. Add regression tests for >12 pending changes and for a change arriving between ask and answer.

findings.title: A device can keep postponing the workstation review indefinitely by writing between each ask and answer
findings.scenario: Each device-authored project write between a desktop review ask and its answer makes the workstation's allow_once throw and re-ask (manager.server.ts:2335 and 3580-3583). A device that keeps writing can keep every answer stale, so the workstation never completes the review. This is an availability issue only; it cannot make code run without an answer, but it wedges the approval flow. Confirmed once in the probe (first answer rejected, re-ask created).
findings.evidence: Probe second run: 'R1 answer result: Project files changed after this request was raised; a fresh request lists the changes.' followed by a new request id. Repeated device writes would produce repeated rejections.
findings.recommendation: Allow a bounded number of stale re-asks, or let the workstation answer the current list in one step, and surface to the user that the device is still changing files.

findings.title: Device one-time approval launches a tool-free session past the Mission provider-session budget
findings.scenario: A Mission step's Ollama (tool-free) route is refused by launchModel because taskViolation returns 'provider-session budget exhausted' (authorization.server.ts:467, sessionsUsed >= maxSessions). launchModel turns that into a provider.execute ask with desktopRequired unset (manager.server.ts:1431-1449). deviceRequestRefusal's provider.execute branch (2035-2040) answers it for any task where deviceMayLaunch is true, whatever the violation reason. A paired device then calls mission.respond allow_once (commands.server.ts / http.server.ts), which goes to respond() -> tasks.approve() -> launch() -> missionScopeCheck('check'/'launch') (manager.server.ts:97-127). That check runs providerScopeViolation, agenticProviderCheck and the codex exclusion only. It never re-runs taskViolation's budget, execution, providers.allow or localOnly checks. The session launches, and countModelCall (manager.server.ts:1480) runs only on the launchModel success path, so device-approved sessions are never counted and each retry can be re-approved. Repro (probed): mission with one read model step, localOnly, maxRetries 0, approved by a phone without start; store envelope providers.sessions.maxSessions forced to 0 to reach the real violation branch; phone mission.start -> ask 'ollama for Writer: provider-session budget exhausted' with desktopRequired undefined; phone mission.respond allow_once -> one ollama/test-local session launched.
findings.evidence: Probe PROBE-A in a throwaway folder: output 'PROBE-A ask: ollama for Writer: provider-session budget exhausted desktopRequired= undefined' and 'PROBE-A launched sessions: [ ollama/test-local ] budget maxSessions=0'; the assertion that the session must not launch failed. Relevant code: authorization.server.ts:462-468 (taskViolation budget branch, only reached from launchModel and admitAgenticProvider), manager.server.ts:114-126 (missionScopeCheck has no budget check), 1417-1451 (launchModel ask), 2035-2040 (device allowance), 3652-3656 (respond approve path), host manager.server.ts:1127-1131 (final scope check). Impact is bounded to tool-free local inference (no shell or code execution), but it breaks the 'actions outside the reviewed envelope' rule for devices and can be repeated indefinitely.
findings.recommendation: Make the launch-time re-check for a provider session include taskViolation's budget, execution, providers.allow and localOnly checks, or refuse device answers to a provider.execute ask whose violation is not the route-authority ceiling (deviceRequestRefusal should require the same taskViolation to be empty for the exact task). Also count device-approved sessions in mission.accounting so a budget cannot be exceeded silently.

findings.title: Review gate and launch-phase check are inconsistent: launch phase skips the review gate for workstation envelopes
findings.scenario: missionScopeCheck(task, 'launch') returns null for every non-remote envelope before the pending-review check at line 115 runs. Current call sites are safe because each 'launch' is preceded by a 'check' in the same synchronous run (host manager.server.ts:1129->1136 and the startSession chain at 1286->1288). Any future caller that invokes phase 'launch' alone would skip the Host-wide review gate for workstation envelopes.
findings.evidence: manager.server.ts:105-107 early return; 115-116 review gate placed after it; host manager.server.ts:1135-1137 and 1286-1288 call order.
findings.recommendation: Run the pending-review check before the phase branch, or assert in the launch phase that the same task was checked in this run.

findings.title: Direct (non-Mission) provider sessions and direct capability runs are outside the Host-wide review gate
findings.scenario: The review gate in CapabilityBus.decision is skipped for request.direct, and missionScopeCheck runs only for mission tasks (host manager.server.ts:1046-1051 and 1128-1131). A workstation-approved non-Mission shell session or direct terminal run can therefore execute in a folder with unacknowledged paired-device changes without a review prompt. The workstation is the approver, so this is not a device-authority escalation, but it differs from the stated 'wherever it runs' wording in round 4.
findings.evidence: bus.server.ts review gate condition uses !request.direct; manager.server.ts missionScopeCheck is attached only to mission children.
findings.recommendation: Confirm owner intent. If the review gate should cover direct runs too, add a pending-review prompt to the direct path.

result.reasoning:
Not refuted. The carry-over path is real and I could not find a precondition that blocks it.

Chain, verified by reading the code:
1. Execute-phase device judgement (manager.server.ts ~2054-2058) only checks the executor's params, via agenticRequestParams. A verification check on the same action is not judged.
2. respond() sets step.approvedOnce = {requestId, action: 'filesystem.read'} (manager.server.ts ~3702).
3. The execute run goes straight to verifyAndComplete (~2931 and ~4015 call sites). Nothing clears approvedOnce on the way (setStep to 'verifying' at ~2962 only changes state). The clearing sites at ~3160, ~3846, ~3855, ~4099 are completion, Retry and restart paths.
4. For verification check B, capabilityRequest (~1520) sets oneTimeAction = 'filesystem.read'. bus.server.ts:174 then sets oneTime = true.
5. The Host-side checks before decide do not block it. remoteExecutionRefusal('filesystem.read') returns null (probe). agenticCheck falls through to projectResourceCheck, which only rejects 'sensitive' paths (.env, .ssh, keys, etc.) or paths inside another registered project. C:/Windows/win.ini is neither, so it returns null. The bus gates for mutations and runsCode do not apply to reads.
6. decide() returns allow at authorization.server.ts:354 before scopeViolation (~367).

Probe (throwaway temp dir, deleted afterwards; no repo files touched, no repo tests run): decide() with a remote envelope (authority kind remote, grantedBy device:phone-1, projectRoots [proj-root]) and filesystem.read of C:/Windows/win.ini. oneTime=false returns ask "outside the approved read scope". oneTime=true returns allow. Adding an ask_every_time grant with oneTime=true still returns allow.

Preconditions: the device answer on the execute step needs an ask on a READ action, which only happens with an explicit ask_every_time rule on filesystem.read. Verification READ checks are not root-scoped at plan approval (planner.server.ts ~148 and manager.server.ts ~701-712 check READ/non-sensitive only), and scopeFor (authorization.server.ts ~37-70) adds only the project root. So the plan can carry an out-of-root read check. The workstation would be asked for that read if no device answer had carried over.

Impact: no code execution, read-only, and the device acts outside the reviewed envelope. That falls under the owner policy's "actions outside the reviewed envelope" prohibition. Not a listed disposition: the one-time-ask disposition covers the exact planned in-envelope step, and the verify check here is out-of-envelope. Disclosure to the device is limited to what Mission views expose (at least the pass/fail result).

Suggested fix as in the finding: judge same-action verification checks in the execute-phase candidate set too, or clear approvedOnce when entering 'verifying' for a device answer.</reasoning>

Not refuted. I verified both manifestations by reading the code paths; I did not rerun the probes, and I edited nothing and ran no repo tests.

(a) Truncation. bus.server.ts:169-170 builds the ask reason from the Host-wide pending paths, truncated to 12 with "and N more", and sets remoteReview to all pending ids. manager.server.ts:2271-2273 (pendingRemoteReview) returns every unacknowledged change id. manager.server.ts:3378 truncates the mission-level list the same way. respond() at 3593-3594 then acknowledges all of request.remoteReview on allow_once. So the workstation is told "and N more" without the names, and every hidden id is marked reviewed. The approver is told there are unseen changes, which makes this an informed-consent defect rather than a silent omission, and it does not depend on the device.

(b) Superseded re-ask. manager.server.ts:3580-3583 re-asks with reason = request.reason.split(" Files changed in this Mission under paired-device authority")[0]. The old bus reason never contains that marker, so the stale 12-path text is kept. remoteReview is then reset to the full current pending id list. askPermission (3376-3378) appends only the mission-level list, which comes from remoteChanges (2250-2258). That list filters to succeeded runs of this Mission, so in-flight or failed changes and changes from other Missions are never shown, yet pendingRemoteReview includes them. R2 can therefore carry acknowledged ids that its text never names, and respond() at 3594 acknowledges them. The mintDesktopGrant binding (3347-3360) is refreshed for R2, so the grant itself is valid; only the disclosure is wrong.

Mitigations considered: the workstation still has to click allow_once, and the operation (e.g., "node build.mjs") names the script, so the approver could have inspected it. That does not cure the defect: the review gate's stated purpose is that code never runs over device changes the workstation was shown, and acknowledgment records the opposite. Acknowledged ids are also never re-prompted for the same content. This is not a device-only path to code execution (the workstation must approve), so I rate it HIGH rather than BLOCKER. It is not one of the listed owner-policy dispositions or accepted limitations.

Confirmed manifestation (b), superseded re-ask:

Why it is not an owner-policy disposition: the owner dispositions cover device one-time answers for exact in-envelope steps and the classifier denylist, not the review gate's disclosure. The gate records acknowledgement for changes the approver was never shown, so a device-authored file can then be executed after a workstation allow_once. Core claim confirmed by a probe in a mkdtemp folder (deleted afterwards; no repo files touched, no repo tests run). Setup: a non-Agent Mission with one read model step, localOnly, maxRetries 0, approved by a device with start=false; envelope providers.sessions.maxSessions forced to 0 via store.saveAuthorization; device mission.start. Result: ask "ollama for Writer: provider-session budget exhausted" with desktopRequired and remoteReview both undefined (launchModel, manager.server.ts ~1431-1449). Device mission.respond allow_once returned ok and launched ollama/test-local. Code path confirmed: deviceRequestRefusal provider.execute branch (manager.server.ts ~2035-2040) checks only deviceMayLaunch (tool-free/local), not the taskViolation reason. respond -> tasks.approve -> launch -> missionScopeCheck("check"/"launch") (manager.server.ts 97-127) never evaluates the sessionsUsed budget in taskViolation (authorization.server.ts:467). The budget is part of the reviewed authorization envelope, so a device acting past it is outside the owner policy's envelope rule, even though impact is confined to tool-free local inference (no shell or code execution, so not BLOCKER/HIGH).
Corrections to the finding: (1) its claim that device-approved sessions are never counted is wrong. Direct approval goes through childApprovedDirectly, which calls countModelCall (manager.server.ts ~2830), and the probe's accounting showed localModelCalls=1 after the device launch. (2) "Repeated indefinitely" is overstated. mission.retry is not in the remote command set (commands.server.ts REMOTE excludes it), so repeats need step-level auto-retries, each producing a fresh ask that a device could answer, bounded by the step's retry count. (3) Related, unreported in the finding: the admission closure in admitAgenticProvider (manager.server.ts ~2770-2782) and the Host launch path call taskViolation without the sessionsUsed argument (default 0), so the session budget is enforced only at launchModel ask time, for Agent Missions too.
Recommendation stands in substance: refuse device answers to provider.execute asks whose violation is anything other than the tool-free route ceiling, or re-run the budget check at launch for device actors. Severity kept at MEDIUM on policy grounds; LOW would also be defensible given the bounded impact.

The stale-answer path is real as described: manager.server.ts:2335 throws DesktopRequestStale when asked.mutationSequence !== bindings.mutationSequence, and manager.server.ts:3580-3583 denies the superseded request and re-asks with the current pending review ids. So the code behaves as the finding says, but the finding does not show a security problem. (1) The check fails closed: a stale answer never mints a grant, and the re-ask shows the workstation the current changes, which is the intended property. (2) The trigger is not device-specific. store.server.ts:150 counts every capability_runs row with a mutating action (filesystem.write/delete, git.commit/merge, worktree add/remove, browser.download, terminal.exec), whatever actor produced it, so the Host's own Agent writes also make answers stale. (3) A device cannot postpone indefinitely on its own. Each device-driven cycle needs an approved planned write step inside the Mission envelope, and the Agent must raise a fresh ask after each one, so repetition is bounded by the reviewed plan. (4) The device already holds pause/stop within its authority (policy), which wedges the Mission more strongly than repeated stale rejections do, so the device gains no authority it lacks. What remains is an availability and UX nuisance with no code execution and no action outside the envelope. I did not run a probe; the verdict rests on reading the code paths named above.

Verified by reading the code; the mechanism is real but it is availability-only and the "indefinitely" wording is overstated. Not refuted, LOW.

Mechanism confirmed:
- manager.server.ts:2332-2335 (mintDesktopGrant) throws DesktopRequestStale when asked.mutationSequence !== the current mutationSequence.
- manager.server.ts:3576-3583 catches that, resolves the old request as deny with resolvedBy "(superseded: project changed)", and re-asks with the current pending review ids. The throw is then rethrown as CommandRefusedError, so no grant is minted and no code runs.
- store.server.ts:150-153: mutationSequence() is a host-wide COUNT of capability_runs rows with mutating actions, including failed runs. So any such run bumps it, not only device writes, and the workstation's own runs also invalidate pending asks.

Why it stays LOW, and why "indefinitely" is wrong:
- Device writes can only land as exact planned steps inside the Mission envelope (owner policy), and the plan is finite. Retry is not a device action (owner policy), so the device cannot generate unbounded writes to keep the sequence moving. The stall is bounded by plan step count.
- No security boundary is crossed. A stale answer is refused, not granted. The device cannot cause execution or widen the envelope through this path.
- The workstation can still complete the review by answering the fresh request once no further mutation lands, or by stopping or revoking the device envelope.

I did not run a probe or the test file for this refutation; the verdict rests on code reading. No repo files were touched, and no test-results/ files were changed by this review.

findings.title: Review acknowledgment covers paired-device changes the workstation was never shown
findings.scenario: Device-authored changes beyond the 12 displayed paths are acknowledged by a routine workstation allow_once, so device-authored code then runs under the approval. Repro: a paired device runs two phone-approved Missions: mission A writes 12 decoy files (aa-01..aa-12.txt), mission B writes zz-13.mjs (content writes pwned.txt). Pending remote changes = 13. The workstation approves terminal.exec 'node entry.mjs' (entry.mjs imports ./zz-13.mjs). The ask reason lists 12 paths then 'and 1 more' and never names zz-13.mjs. Workstation allow_once acknowledges all 13 ids, pendingRemoteChanges drops to 0, and the run completes with pwned.txt = 'device-authored code ran'.
findings.evidence: Probed (throwaway script, OS temp, deleted). bus.server.ts:169-170 sets remoteReview: review.ids (all pending ids) while the reason shows review.paths.slice(0, 12). manager.server.ts:2272-2273 returns all pending ids and paths. manager.server.ts:3594 acknowledges every request.remoteReview id on allow_once. The same truncation exists at manager.server.ts:1430 (launch reviewViolation) and manager.server.ts:3376-3378 (remoteChanges display). Probe 1: 13 pending -> reason tail 'unseen-12.txt and 1 more' -> after allow_once pending=0. Probe 2 as above: state completed, pwned.txt present. Policy impact: the owner disposition relies on the Host-wide review gate to backstop the denylist classifier; this gate can be satisfied without the approver seeing the changed file.
findings.recommendation: Acknowledge only the ids actually displayed, and refuse allow_once (or require an explicit full review) while pending changes exceed the displayed list. Prefer listing all pending paths (paginated or full) in the ask. Code runs must stay blocked until every pending id is acknowledged, so the unseen remainder fails closed rather than being acknowledged.

findings.title: Execution-config classifier omits common tool configs that run code when loaded
findings.scenario: Under remote authority a device-approved ordinary write to a tool config that a workstation-approved tool later loads is classified as ordinary and allowed. It is then gated only by the Host-wide review gate, which finding 1 weakens. Example: a device writes vitest.workspace.ts (or .babelrc, turbo.json) as the hidden 13th change; a later approved 'npm test' or build loads it.
findings.evidence: Probed with executionConfigPath and remoteExecutionRefusal('filesystem.write', ...) for vitest.workspace.ts, .babelrc, turbo.json, Pipfile, lerna.json, .mcp.json, .claude/settings.json and opencode.json: executionConfigPath=false and remote refusal=null for all of them. vitest.config.ts, package.json and .git/config are correctly refused. EXECUTION_CONFIG_FILE is at authorization.server.ts:123 and EXECUTION_CONFIG_DIR at line 124. Claude read launches use --setting-sources '' and --strict-mcp-config (adapters.server.ts:406-407), so the .claude/.mcp.json vectors do not apply to read sessions. Impact is defense-in-depth, not a direct bypass on its own.
findings.recommendation: Add vitest.workspace.*, .babelrc*, turbo.json, lerna.json, nx.json, Pipfile, .mcp.json, opencode.json and the .claude/.codex/.cursor/.opencode directories to the classifier. Better, treat any new repo-root or dot-config file as execution-config by default, and fix finding 1 so the review gate is complete.

findings.title: Superseded desktop re-ask keeps the stale operation binding, so approval can never match
findings.scenario: A desktop ask is superseded because the project changed. The re-ask passes the old request (with its ask-time desktopOperation, including terminal file digests) into askPermission, and the workstation's later allow_once mints a grant bound to that stale operation. If the superseding change touched the script, the fresh operation digest differs at execution and the grant is refused as 'differs from the one authorized'.
findings.evidence: Code reading, not probed. manager.server.ts:3578-3583 passes { ...request, remoteReview } as the desktop argument to askPermission. askPermission (about lines 3391-3396) copies desktop.desktopOperation into the new request. mintDesktopGrant (manager.server.ts:2326-2330) binds request.desktopOperation rather than recomputing it. desktopGrantViolation then fails on operation mismatch (authorization.server.ts desktopGrantViolation, last check). The refusal is fail-closed and a fresh ask follows, so the cost is an extra approval.
findings.recommendation: Recompute desktopOperation for the re-ask (capabilityOperation or sessionOperation) rather than reusing the superseded one.

findings.title: One-time allowance short-circuits scope and ask-every-time checks and is keyed only by action
findings.scenario: A device-answered one-time for a READ or WRITE capability in a non-Agent Mission covers later same-action requests in that step, including verification checks on other paths. decide() returns allow for oneTime (line 354) before the ask_every_time check (364) and scopeViolation (367).
findings.evidence: Code reading, not probed. oneTimeAction is action-only (manager.server.ts:1520). Verification capability checks must be READ (manager.server.ts:706), so no write spill is possible. Device answers do not extend roots (manager.server.ts:1507), and the filesystem adapter confines reads to context.roots, which limits real impact. Agent Missions are protected by a fingerprint check on oneTimeAction (manager.server.ts around 2589-2600).
findings.recommendation: Key the one-time allowance to the exact fingerprint (action plus params plus cwd), not action only, or re-run scopeViolation and ask_every_time checks for oneTime requests.

result.reasoning:
Not refuted. Static trace confirms the mechanism; I did not run the end-to-end probe (no Host instance built, per the strict rules), so the claim rests on code reading.

Confirmed path:
- bus.server.ts:169-170: the review ask sets remoteReview: review.ids (every pending id, from manager.server.ts:2271-2273 via store.pendingRemoteChanges(), which returns all unacknowledged rows with no cap), but the reason text shows only review.paths.slice(0, 12) plus "and N more". Unseen paths are never named.
- manager.server.ts:3593-3594: on allow_once by a trusted-local actor, acknowledgeRemoteChanges(request.remoteReview) marks every id acknowledged. store.server.ts:161-164 does this with no check that the approver saw them. The acknowledgement is persistent (acknowledged_at is set), so the unseen file stops gating future code runs too.
- The same truncation appears at manager.server.ts:1430 (session launch) and 3376-3378 (display). The 3376 list is per-Mission only, so it does not cover Host-wide pending changes either.

Why it is not refuted: the round-4 invariant (C) is "code never runs over paired-device changes the workstation has not reviewed". With 13 pending, zz-13.mjs is acknowledged and code runs over it without the workstation having been shown it. A device-authored file under an approval the workstation granted on incomplete information breaks the owner-stated backstop for the denylist classifier. The "and 1 more" text does disclose that more exist, which limits severity; a human still has to click allow_once, and the approver sees only paths, not contents, even for the 12 shown. I therefore rate it HIGH rather than BLOCKER. Not one of the listed owner dispositions or accepted limitations.

Fix direction matches the finding: acknowledge only displayed ids, or refuse allow_once while pending exceeds the displayed list.

Refutation attempted and failed; the finding holds on code reading. No probe was run and no repo file or test was touched.

Confirmed mechanics:
- src/lib/bunny-missions/capabilities/bus.server.ts:168-170: the review gate returns remoteReview: review.ids (every pending id) while the reason text shows only review.paths.slice(0, 12) plus "and N more".
- src/lib/bunny-missions/manager.server.ts:2271-2273 (pendingRemoteReview) returns all pending ids and paths, with no truncation of ids.
- src/lib/bunny-missions/store.server.ts:158-159 orders pending changes by `at`, so the newest, unlisted change is the one that falls past the 12-path display cut.
- src/lib/bunny-missions/manager.server.ts:3593-3594: on allow_once by a trusted-local actor, acknowledgeRemoteChanges(request.remoteReview) acknowledges every id, including the ones never shown in the reason.
- Nothing else renders the full pending list. The grep of src/components and src/routes found no remoteReview usage, so the workstation's only review surface is the truncated reason text.

Preconditions hold: a device may legitimately write bounded files inside a Mission envelope (policy-allowed), and terminal.exec is runsCode, so the gate applies. A 13th unseen change lets the workstation's single allow_once clear the whole pending set, so code runs over a file the human was never shown. This contradicts the stated invariant "code never runs over paired-device changes the workstation has not reviewed".

Severity stays HIGH, not BLOCKER: a device cannot start code itself. Execution still requires a workstation allow_once, but that approval rests on incomplete information the Host presents as the complete review. The same truncation also exists at manager.server.ts:1429-1430 (session reviewViolation) and manager.server.ts:3376-3377 (remoteChanges display), so the recommended fix should cover all three sites.

Refuted as a listed owner-policy disposition: "the execution-config classifier is a denylist by design, backed by the Host-wide review gate." The regex gap is real. The claimed chain therefore needs the workstation to approve a code run that displays the pending path, which is the designed gate. I did not run a probe. The finding is refuted as a reportable issue because it is exactly the owner-policy disposition "the execution-config classifier is a denylist by design, backed by the Host-wide review gate". I probed in a temp folder (since deleted, no repo files touched, no test-results change): executionConfigPath and remote refusal return false/null for vitest.workspace.ts, vitest.workspace.mts, .babelrc, turbo.json, lerna.json, nx.json, Pipfile, .mcp.json, .claude/settings.json, opencode.json and src/app.ts. They return refusal for vitest.config.ts, package.json, .git/config, jest.config.ts, babel.config.js and webpack.config.js. The gap is therefore a denylist omission, not a path to code execution by a device. Ordinary source such as src/app.ts is equally unclassified, so the gap is not specific to the names listed. The device cannot run code itself: remoteExecutionRefusal blocks terminal.exec and provider sessions, and any later runsCode Mission request while a remote change is unacknowledged asks the workstation with desktopRequired and remoteReview ids (manager.server.ts:2272, 3580-3594). The Host-wide review gate is the backstop the owner accepted. The finding's own evidence calls the impact defense-in-depth. I did not verify the claim that finding 1 weakens the review gate, so that part stands on the other reviewer's finding. Recommendation kept as a hardening note only: extending the denylist (vitest.workspace.*, .babelrc*, turbo.json, .mcp.json, .claude/*) is reasonable, but it is not a finding under the stated policy.

The mechanism is real but the stated impact is overstated, so the finding survives only as a LOW correctness issue.

Confirmed in code (read only, no probe run):
- manager.server.ts:3578-3583 re-asks with `{ ...request, ...(review ? { remoteReview } : {}) }`, so the superseded request's ask-time desktopOperation is carried into askPermission.
- askPermission (~3394) copies desktop.desktopOperation into the new request, while desktopBinding (~3398) is recomputed fresh, including the current mutationSequence.
- mintDesktopGrant (2326-2328) calls desktopContext with request.desktopOperation, so the grant's operation is the stale one.
- desktopGrantViolation (authorization.server.ts:276) then requires sameOperation(grant.operation, fresh op). For terminal.exec, the op includes fileIdentities (file digests), so a superseding change to a script the command runs does produce a mismatch.

Where the headline is wrong:
- The mismatch happens only when the superseding change altered the operation itself. If the change touched an unrelated file, the stale op equals the fresh op and the grant works.
- It is not a permanent block. At execution, bus.server.ts:300 returns a fresh ask carrying a current capabilityOperation when desktopGrantConsume refuses. The grant is not consumed in that refusal path. A new request then gets a fresh binding, so the workstation can approve it.
- No escape: the stale grant can only authorize the stale operation, and execution requires the current operation to equal it. A device cannot mint or reuse grants.

Net effect: one extra workstation approval round trip in the case where the superseding change altered the operation. The fix is still worth making: recompute desktopOperation for the re-ask. The phrase "can never match" should be corrected to "matches only if the operation is unchanged; otherwise one wasted approval".

Test coverage: remote-authority.test.ts:872-900 (F01-R16) covers the superseded re-ask but not a changed operation, so it does not exercise this path. I did not run the test file.

The finding's mechanism is real, but the impact is a fail-closed extra approval cycle, not a security escape.

Verified by code reading (no repo files touched, no tests run, no probes):
- manager.server.ts:3576-3583: on DesktopRequestStale the re-ask passes `{ ...request, remoteReview }` into askPermission. `request.desktopOperation` is the ask-time operation, carried over unchanged. askPermission (about manager.server.ts:3391-3396) copies `desktop.desktopOperation` into the new request and builds a fresh desktopBinding from the current mutationSequence.
- manager.server.ts:2326-2328 (mintDesktopGrant) takes `operation` from `desktopContext(..., request.desktopOperation)`, so a grant minted from the re-ask carries the stale operation. Its mutationSequence, taskId and authorizationId come from the current context, so only the operation field is stale.
- authorization.server.ts:245-258 (capabilityOperation): for terminal.exec the operation includes `files` digests from fileIdentities. The digest is computed at ask time. If the superseding change edited a file the command names, the fresh digest differs and sameOperation in desktopGrantViolation (authorization.server.ts ~277) returns "differs from the one authorized on the desktop". For non-terminal actions the stale op only matches if params are unchanged, so the failure is narrower than "never".
- bus.server.ts:298-300: at execution a violation returns decision "ask" with a freshly computed capabilityOperation. The grant is not consumed (consumeDesktopGrant returns before incrementing uses), and the step gets a new ask through result.permission (manager.server.ts ~1566-1580). The next approval uses a fresh operation, so the Mission does not stay stuck, though I did not trace the step-level re-ask in full.

No path lets a device or a stale grant run anything the workstation did not approve for that exact operation: sameOperation and the mutation-sequence check still gate execution. The defect is that one workstation allow_once can be wasted, which is correctness at LOW. The recommendation (recompute desktopOperation for the re-ask) is sound. Line numbers in the finding are approximate: the re-ask call is at 3582-3583.
